newsitem.title: EGYPT: Gas field found off Egyptian north coast.
newsitem.headline: Gas field found off Egyptian north coast.

text.p: Petrobel, a joint venture between the Egyptian state and International Egyptian Oil Company (IEOC) of Italy, has found a gas field in the El Qara concession off the northern coast of Egypt, the oil ministry said on Tuesday.
The concession belongs to IEOC (50 percent), Amoco (25 percent) and USX Marathon (25 percent). IEOC is a unit of the Italian company AGIP SpA.
An exploratory well, Nidoco 9, found a gas-bearing layer 30 metres thick at a depth of 3,400 metres and Petrobel estimates that it will produce 30 million cubic feet a day.
"The well will soon be connected and then we can test it. The 30 million cubic feet is an estimate based on past experience," said an oil company executive.
The ministry said the well was three km (two miles) offshore and 17 km (11 miles) northeast of the coastal town of Baltim.

The oil company executive, who declined to be named, said it was in a new field and that the nearest fields were the onshore El Qara field in the same concession and the Baltim offshore field in the adjacent Baltim concession, which belongs to IEOC (50 percent) and Amoco (50 percent).
Recent exploration in the Mediterranean off the Nile Delta has produced a spate of gas discoveries. Oil companies are describing it as a gas zone of international significance.
